around.headline: Speeding car kills scooter rider, damages three more vehicles in signal-side crash at Kaggadasapura
around.summary: A speeding car (reported as a Baleno/MUV) rammed a scooter at a traffic signal in Kaggadasapura today, killing the rider — a hairstylist — and damaging three other vehicles in the pile-up; the driver has been arrested, per today's reports. If you're on a two-wheeler, glance at your mirrors while stopped at a signal so a fast-approaching vehicle doesn't catch you off guard.
around.source: Deccan Herald, NDTV, The Times of India

around.headline: Six held for killing medical shop owner on Madiwala Main Road
around.summary: Police have arrested six people over the daylight killing of a shop owner on Madiwala Main Road reported earlier this week, per today's report. A reminder that CCTV and witness footage are increasingly what turns these cases into quick arrests.

around.headline: Traffic diversions across Bengaluru on August 26 for the Eid Milad-un-Nabi procession
around.summary: Police have confirmed route diversions and curbs on heavy vehicles for Wednesday's Milad-un-Nabi procession, including JC Road and KG Road, per today's reports. Check the diversion map before driving through the city centre tomorrow.
around.source: The Hindu, Deccan Herald, The Economic Times

around.headline: State minister red-flags DK Shivakumar's Bengaluru parking-fee proposal
around.summary: Transport minister Ramalinga Reddy has urged the Karnataka CM to reconsider a proposed parking fee on Bengaluru residents, calling it a burden on citizens, per today's reports. Worth watching if you park on the street or in paid civic lots — the fee isn't final yet.

around.headline: 46.88 lakh names flagged for deletion in Bengaluru's SIR draft voter roll
around.summary: Today's draft electoral roll under the Special Intensive Revision flags 46.88 lakh names across Bengaluru for possible deletion, per today's report. If you haven't already, check your name in the draft roll and file a correction before the objection window closes.

around.headline: Government clears transfer of DRDO missile technology to local industry
around.summary: The government has approved transferring DRDO missile technology to private manufacturers in a push to boost domestic defence production, per today's report. Bengaluru's large aerospace and defence manufacturing base makes this a sector to watch for hiring and vendor tenders in the months ahead.

street_smart.title: You're stopped on your two-wheeler at a red signal when you glance in your mirror and see a car coming up fast, clearly not slowing down — like today's Kaggadasapura crash where a speeding car killed a scooter rider and hit three more vehicles at a signal. You have maybe two seconds. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real report: a speeding car rammed a scooter at a signal in Kaggadasapura, killing the rider and damaging three other vehicles; the driver was arrested (Deccan Herald, NDTV, The Times of India). This scenario focuses on the split-second choice a rider or pedestrian has when they spot the danger just before impact.
street_smart.situation: There's cross traffic moving on the green light to your right, and vehicles stopped on either side of you leave little room to move.

choices.text: Immediately steer toward any open gap — footpath edge, shoulder, or space between stopped vehicles — rather than staying in the car's direct path.
choices.feedback: Correct — in the one or two seconds you have, moving out of the vehicle's line of travel matters far more than anything else. A moving target that's off the car's path is much harder to hit than one that stays still hoping the driver brakes in time.

choices.text: Gun it through the red light into the cross traffic to get clear of the danger behind you.
choices.feedback: This is the trap — cross traffic has the green light and isn't expecting anyone to enter from your direction. You'd be swapping a threat you can see for one you can't, and you're also now the one running the red.

choices.text: Stay put and honk or wave to alert the driver behind you.
choices.feedback: A driver who's already too fast to stop in time is unlikely to react to a horn in under two seconds. Standing still and hoping to be noticed wastes the small window you have to actually move.

choices.text: Get off the bike and try to run clear on foot.
choices.feedback: Dismounting takes time you don't have, and a moving bike (even a short shove sideways) usually clears more distance faster than someone scrambling off it. If there's truly no gap to steer into, staying low and bracing is a last resort — not abandoning the vehicle mid-signal.

takeaways: At a signal, periodically check your mirrors — spotting a fast-approaching vehicle two seconds earlier is often the difference between reacting and not.
When something dangerous is behind you, the safe move is almost always lateral — into a gap — not forward into traffic that has the right of way.

If you witness or are involved in a hit-and-run, note the plate number or get a photo immediately — CCTV plus a witness's plate photo is what usually leads to a fast arrest, as it did in today's Madiwala case.

quiz.question: How many names were flagged for possible deletion in Bengaluru's SIR draft voter roll, per today's report?
quiz.why: The flagged names fall under the ASDD category — Absent, Shifted, Dead, or Duplicate — and need verification before the final electoral roll is published.

quiz.question: Which minister urged the Karnataka CM to reconsider the proposed Bengaluru parking fee, per today's reports?
quiz.why: Ramalinga Reddy holds the state's Transport portfolio, making parking and road-use policy directly part of his remit.

quiz.question: Traffic diversions are in place across Bengaluru on August 26 for which occasion?
quiz.why: The procession marking the Prophet Muhammad's birth anniversary draws large crowds through the city centre, prompting curbs on heavy vehicles along the route.

quiz.question: Nitrogen makes up roughly what share of Earth's atmosphere by volume?
quiz.why: Oxygen, the gas most associated with breathing, makes up only about 21% — nitrogen is the atmosphere's largest component by far.

quiz.question: In Indian monetary policy, the 'repo rate' is the rate at which:
options: Banks lend to each other overnight
The RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
The government borrows from foreign investors
Banks charge customers on credit cards
quiz.why: When the RBI raises the repo rate, banks' own borrowing costs rise, and that increase typically gets passed on as higher loan and EMI rates for consumers.
